Inside the documentation ↗
ProductController.phpPHP
<?php

namespace App\Controllers;

use Zephyrus\Controller\Controller;
use Zephyrus\Http\Response;
use Zephyrus\Routing\Attribute\Get;

final class ProductController extends Controller
{
    #[Get('/products/{id}')]
    public function show(int $id): Response
    {
        return Response::json(['id' => $id]);
    }
}
<?php

use Zephyrus\Http\Response;

// JSON, with an explicit status.
$response = Response::json([
    'id' => 42,
    'name' => 'Something worth building',
], 201);

// Immutable objects. Intentional changes.
$response = $response->withHeader(
    'Cache-Control', 'no-store'
);

return $response;

<?php

use stdClass;
use Zephyrus\Data\Broker;

final class ProductBroker extends Broker
{
    public function find(int $id): ?stdClass
    {
        return $this->selectOne(
            'SELECT id, name FROM product WHERE id = ?',
            [$id]
        );
    }
}

03 / A COHERENT FOUNDATIONFOLLOW THE REQUEST.

Every part.
In its place.

One considered path through your application.
Explore the pieces that make it work.

REQUESTRESPONSEDESIGNED TO WORK TOGETHER.
01Routing & controllers

PHP attributes connect a URL to a controller method. Typed parameters bring the request into your code with a clear contract.

Explore routing ↗
02Immutable HTTP

Request and response objects keep their state. Changes return a new object, making each step easier to follow.

Explore HTTP ↗
03Security & validation

Security middleware and validation rules give your application a shared place to handle boundaries and incoming data.

Explore security ↗
04Typed configuration

YAML configuration, environment values and typed sections keep application settings visible and organized.

Explore configuration ↗
05JSON localization

Split translations across JSON files. Nested keys, parameters and formatting pipes keep messages readable. Regional locales fall back to their language, then the configured default.

Explore localization ↗
06SQL, in plain sight

Brokers group explicit SQL and bound parameters by domain. Typed query helpers, composable transactions and Entity hydration keep the data path visible.

Explore data access ↗
04 / CHOICES THAT MATTERLOOK A LITTLE CLOSER.

Control where
it counts.

A few deliberate choices inside the core. Useful when an application grows, changes roles or starts talking in real time.

01 / RUNTIME ROLES

One codebase. Several entry points.

Use RequiresEnv on a controller or method to register its routes only when an environment value matches. Web and API roles can share application code while exposing their own routes.

#[RequiresEnv('MODE', 'API')]
02 / DEPENDENCY INJECTION

A small container. Explicit wiring.

Autowire constructor dependencies, bind interfaces and choose which services are shared. Circular dependencies are detected during resolution.

bind() / singleton() / make()
03 / COMPOSABLE ACCESS

Access rules you can combine.

Compose guards with all, any and not logic, then apply them through middleware. The same core also supplies CSRF, CSP and secure-header middleware.

AllAuthGuard / AnyAuthGuard / NotAuthGuard
04 / EVENT STREAMING

A generator. A live conversation.

Stream Server-Sent Events from a PHP generator. Typed SseEvent messages carry data, event names, IDs and retry values, with multiline data handled for you.

Generator → SseEvent → SseEmitter
